name: Chungdi Malai
subtitle: prawns simmered in coconut milk, mildly spiced and faintly sweet, Odisha's most coaxing curry

ingredients.qty: 500g medium, shelled and deveined, tails on

ingredients.note: the traditional fat here; use oil if you prefer

prepNotes: Rub the shelled prawns with 1/4 tsp turmeric and 1/2 tsp salt and rest 10 minutes. Rinse and pat dry before cooking.
Grind the onion to a smooth paste with no water. Wet onion paste will not brown properly and the gravy stays raw-tasting.
Shake the tin of coconut milk before opening, and keep it out of the fridge — cold coconut milk splits when it hits a hot pan.

steps.text: Heat 1 tbsp ghee in a kadhai and sear the prawns on high for 45 seconds a side, until they just turn pink. Lift them out at once.
steps.tip: Prawns cook in under two minutes total. Anything more and they go to rubber, so undercook them here — they finish in the gravy.

steps.text: Add the remaining 2 tbsp ghee and drop in the bay leaves, cinnamon, cardamom and cloves. Fry 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the onion paste and fry on medium for 8-10 minutes, stirring often, until it turns pale gold and stops smelling raw.
steps.tip: This is the longest step and the one people cut short. Wait for the paste to pull away from the pan in a mass.

steps.text: Stir in the ginger and garlic pastes and cook 2 minutes more.
Add the turmeric, kashmiri chilli and salt with 2 tbsp water and fry 1 minute so the spices do not scorch.
Lower the flame and pour in the coconut milk. Add the sugar and slit green chillies.
steps.tip: Never boil coconut milk hard — it separates into oil and curds. Hold it at a bare simmer.

steps.text: Simmer gently, uncovered, for 6-8 minutes until the gravy thickens enough to coat a spoon.
Return the prawns with any juices, add the garam masala, and simmer 2 minutes only.
Take off the heat and rest 5 minutes covered before serving with plain rice.

storage: Keeps 2 days refrigerated. Reheat on a low flame just until warm — reboiling both splits the coconut milk and toughens the prawns.
